newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally on auction hopes, foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally on auction hopes, foreigners.

text.p: Mexican stocks rallied Tuesday as domestic and foreign investors combed the market for bargains, promted by expectations of plunging primary interest rates.

"It came sooner and quicker than we expected, but a December rally had been on the cards for a while. Stock prices are cheap, political factors have been holding them back," said Daniel Romo, research director at the Bancrecer bank.
The blue chip IPC index soared 85.37 points, or 2.58 percent, to 3,396.44. Volume was heavy at 120.1 million shares traded.

"Foreign buyers came back at last," a trader said. "They seem to have taken profits on the Dow Jones and switched to emerging markets instead. Local stocks look good with primary rates about to fall."

A Reuters survey of money market traders showed they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bill, rates to fall by an average of 1.42 percentage points from last week's auction to 27.66 percent.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile slumped 79.01 points, or 1.21 percent to 6,442.69 points.
On the broad market, 120 stocks changed hands, with gainers trouncing losers by 80 to 21.
Construction stocks Bufete and Tribasa were notable gainers, as were retail stocks like Elektra.
Bufete and Tribasa gained 4.60 (58 cents) and 1.10 pesos (14 cents), respectively, to 52.30 ($3.32) and 22.10 pesos ($2.80). Elektra ended up 2.80 pesos (36 cents) at 64.50 ($8.19).
"These stocks' prices had not moved since before good third-quarter reports. They were cheap," said Roberto Galvan, analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
"We expect construction and retail sectors to benefit from a recovering in domestic consumption," Romo added.

The analysts noted that the bourse broke through one resistance level and was flirting with another at the close which, if broken, would pave the way for a rally to a record high of 3,433 points, and possibly beyond.

Galvan noted that falling Cetes rates at the primary auction -- results of which were due Tuesday evening -- could weaken the peso, but this would make Mexican stocks cheaper in dollar terms and thus more attractive to foreign buyers.
Monday's sudden announcement that Attorney General Antonio Lozano had been fired did cause some pre-open jitters, but those were dashed as bulls stepped to the fore.

"I feel adverse market reaction was soothed by the naming of a successor with a good reputation," said Galvan, referring to Jorge Madrazo, until Monday president of the National Human Rights Commission.
